title: XPI Universal Controller
summary: Shared XPI V2 transport for NSS0 NOR and explicitly initialized NSS1 PSRAM.
features: Four chip-select slots and **16 programmable LUT sequences**; single/dual/quad SDR phases.
NSS0 NOR boot; optional **8 MiB reference PSRAM** on NSS1/GPIO29 ALT0.
Mapped reads and slot-qualified writes, indirect PIO/DMA and status polling; one shared serial engine.
paragraphs: Flash alias and XPI apertures route to one engine. NSS0 retains the boot NOR profile; memory-mapped writes are not a NOR program command. Execute erase/program and PSRAM reconfiguration **from SRAM** with interrupts and other XPI users coordinated.

The selected ESP-PSRAM64H helper reserves slot 1 and LUT sequences 8..11, checks identity and enters QPI before enabling mapped access. Its real 8 MiB range is 0x54000000..0x547FFFFF, inside a 64 MiB slot aperture. The aperture size is not installed capacity. Boot does not depend on this optional RAM.

Software owns the XPI session and provides inactive-high NSS1 bias. A clock change or reset invalidates that session; stop all users and **reinitialize before publishing buffers**. Missing or unrecognized devices leave the mapped slot disabled; cleanup timeout requires coordinated recovery.

The reviewed reference profile uses SCK=MEM/2, six read dummy clocks and bounded CS timing. Direct PSRAM DMA uses aligned 32-bit words, **at most four-beat bursts** and the configured 1 KiB serial boundary; align four-beat jobs to 16 bytes. These are validated digital/model settings, not a physical part speed grade.
Do not conflate serial-command completion, accepted AXI writes and released software ownership. Drain final bus responses and verify data/guards before reusing a captured or displayed frame.
steps: Identify the actual NOR and configure the supported slot, timing and LUT **while idle**.
Keep the executing service and its working state in SRAM before erase/program.
Configure source/destination ranges and the supported DMA request, then start and use a bounded wait.
Inspect engine/FIFO/device status, verify completion and contents as required before making an updated image executable.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: Native SD/SDIO Host (SDIO0)
summary: Native SD/SDIO host with private AXI32 DMA, fabric owner 2.
features: Native 1-bit/4-bit SDR command/data path on GPIO0-5 ALT0.
Private **descriptor-based AXI32 DMA**, external fabric owner 2.
Independent progress and contention with CPU and central DMA.
paragraphs: SDIO0 is a SYS-domain native SD/SDIO host at 0x1000F000. Its private DMA is fabric owner 2; it does not consume a central-DMA request or one of its eight channels.

Follow card identification/enumeration, response and block-transfer rules. The software protocol request is capped at half the actual controller input clock; external-card timing and protocol compliance still require independent qualification.

Descriptor, data and status writeback traffic share the private master. Preserve descriptor and buffer lifetime through **final status/response**, not merely command completion. The accepted P10/SPI-P4 snapshot path uses bounded SRAM bounce buffers to save and read back PSRAM frames; it is not direct PSRAM-to-SDIO DMA or a filesystem.
Card removal, CRC/response errors and timeout require explicit status capture, abort/recovery and ownership cleanup. Do not silently substitute an SPI-mode SD path or advertise a second host.
steps: Select GPIO0-5 and initialize the actual card at a safe protocol rate.
Prepare aligned bounded descriptors/buffers and publish them before start.
Check command, data, DMA and **status writeback completion**; compare readback where required.
On failure drain/recover before descriptors or buffers are reused.
evidence: Source reviewed at the publication SHA. Dated phase evidence retains its own source/profile/stage; no new hardware qualification is implied.

title: On-Chip SRAM
summary: 128 KiB on-chip SRAM; AXI32 data and one APB discovery/counter window.
features: **32 banks of 4 KiB** in the selected profile.
32-bit AXI data, one-bit ID; byte writes and supported memory bursts.
SRAM code, data, BSS and stack; reset does not erase memory.
paragraphs: The Tiny top overrides the reusable SRAM to 128 KiB and 32-bit data. The native memory aperture is 0x30000000 through 0x3001FFFF. APB registers describe the integrated configuration and observations; they are not another storage aperture.

Both reviewed profiles select 32 technology macros of 4 KiB, organized as **four independently serviced 32 KiB groups**. CPU local I/D and external AXI attachments arbitrate at the groups; this is not a single global CPU/DMA lock. Physical area, timing and bank concurrency require their own evidence.

Reset clears control state, **not SRAM contents**. Startup copies initialized sections from Flash and clears BSS explicitly. Stack placement at the SRAM end does not establish a measured maximum stack demand.
steps: Probe memory size, bank count and data width before using a linked image.
Compare ELF/MAP section sizes, buffers and stack margin against the **actual 128 KiB region**.
Use naturally aligned memory transfers and preserve ownership while DMA is active.
Read/reset counters according to their register semantics; reset is not data sanitization.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: General-Purpose Input/Output (GPIO)
summary: 32 physical GPIOs with management and restricted-user register windows.
features: **Atomic set, clear and toggle** outputs; mode, output-enable and open-drain control.
Per-pin interrupts and filtering; alternate functions from the Tiny pin map.
Both windows address the same pads, not two GPIO banks.
paragraphs: GPIO administration controls pad mode, filtering, masks and locks. The restricted window exposes only permitted data/event operations. The **user-access mask starts clear**; grant only the pins required by the application.

Current peripheral routes come from the Tiny topology. UART0 uses GPIO8/9 and I2C0 uses GPIO10/11; retired dedicated UART outputs in the compatibility wrapper are not additional active UARTs. Input CMOS and pull capability are selected by the technology: ICS55 exposes all three capability bits; IHP130 exposes zero.

Before changing a driven alternate function, **disable its producer**, release output enable and use the controller guard/ownership sequence. Electrical drive settings require a reviewed pad/board specification; a register field is not a voltage rating.
steps: Confirm the Tiny alternate-function map and external circuit.
Prepare output data before enabling the driver; set open-drain/pull behavior only as supported by the pad.
Clear observed event causes before enabling the intended interrupt mask.
Use atomic aliases for concurrent updates and apply irreversible locks **only after validation**.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: Direct Memory Access (DMA)
summary: Eight contexts share one AXI32 central-DMA master with memory and stream endpoints.
features: **Eight channels**; direct transfers and **64-byte aligned TCDs**.
32-bit memory transfers, up to 16 beats and 32-word per-channel FIFOs; narrower endpoint limits still apply.
DMA V2.2, request mask 0x000339FF, stream kinds and SPI origin/admission qualification.
paragraphs: Default software leases are UART0=0, I2C0=1, camera=2, serialized bulk=3, Crypto=4/5 and I2S=6/7. Borrow camera DMA2 for memory work only when its owner is inactive.

Enabled requests are software 0, I2S 1/2, XPI 3/4, UART0 5/6, I2C0 7/8, DVP 11, Crypto 12/13 and SPI 16/17. I2C1 9/10 and PIO-lite 14/15 remain absent. SDIO has a separate AXI master rather than a central-DMA request.

**One read and one write** may be outstanding for DMA across independently serviced targets. CPU local SRAM and SDIO can progress at other targets; same-target traffic contends. Burst and wire rates are not sustained application throughput.

TCDs retain the 64-byte layout. Request bits 3:0 use control[15:12]; request bit 4 uses control[25] (RS_DMA_TCD_REQUEST_HIGH). Retain the high bit for SPI16/17 and validate DMA identity, request, kind and endpoint before submission.

SPI pacing admits only the bound channel, matching source/destination port, direction, request and reserved transport credit. Pending descriptor fetch, admission and final response all contribute to ownership. Abort or software timeout does not release channel, descriptor or payload storage until **terminal drain is confirmed**.
PPALite PROCESS uses exact armed direct request 11/DMA2 transfers; processed TCDs are rejected. RAW and the request/channel counts remain unchanged.

The four-bit maximum-burst discovery field **reads zero** when configured 16 is truncated. Actual reusable transport permits 16 beats; PSRAM and SPI impose their own smaller bounds. Preserve this encoding discrepancy separately from the implemented limit.
steps: Reserve channel, endpoints, aligned TCDs and buffers; reject unsupported request/kind/size combinations.
Publish descriptors with memory ordering; configure request and bounded transfer geometry.
Start and wait for the required controller, DMA and bus terminal conditions; inspect byte counts and errors.
On timeout, **keep ownership, abort/drain** according to the endpoint contract, then recover and release explicitly.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: General-Purpose Timers (TIM0, TIM1)
summary: Two 32-bit timer instances with prescalers and interrupt support.
features: Free-running, periodic and one-shot modes.
**16-bit prescalers** and two compare channels per instance.
Debug-freeze integration; no additional advanced timer.
paragraphs: TIM0 and TIM1 share one register definition but have separate base addresses and IRQ bits. Program the selected timer against the **actual committed PCLK** (24 MHz in SAFE24), not the CLINT microsecond timebase.
A delay API has both a requested time interval and a **separate software polling budget**. A zero polling budget or timeout is not proof that a previously running timer stopped.
Use documented status/W1C handling and capture event causes before rearming. Debug halt may stop counting when configured; it does not prevent all register access or provide a system-wide freeze.
steps: **Stop the selected timer** before changing prescale/reload/compare values.
Compute timing from its functional clock and check representable range.
Clear stale events, configure interrupt selection and start.
Acknowledge observed events, recheck pending state and verify stop on recovery.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: Real-Time Clock (RTC)
summary: 64-bit seconds, 1/256-second subsecond time, alarms and wake status.
features: Two alarms, periodic wake and calibration controls.
**Atomic time snapshot** and command/response interface.
AON REF24 timekeeping; independent of SYS switching, but not an independent oscillator.
paragraphs: The managed RTC engine uses **AON REF24 at 24 MHz**. SYS clock changes do not change its timebase. This logical always-on clock domain does not establish battery retention or operation without XIN.

Time reads use the documented snapshot/command sequence. **Poll command completion** before assuming a write has taken effect. Alarm interrupt and wake signals are separate; SYSCTRL exposes both live and sticky wake observations.
Battery-backed retention, oscillator accuracy, calendar drift and deep-sleep operation remain unspecified. A digital counter resolution is not a measured time accuracy.
steps: Probe the engine and configure it against the actual clock.
Set time through the bounded command API and verify completion.
Configure alarm/periodic selections and clear prior causes before enabling events.
Read snapshots consistently and capture wake/IRQ causes **before acknowledgement**.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: Watchdog (WDG)
summary: Window watchdog with early warning and whole-system reset request.
features: AON REF24 watchdog reference; separate from SYS profile switching.
**Two-key service**, window checking and retained reset-cause observation.
Eight watchdog-clock reset-request cycles in this integration.
paragraphs: Configure timing and window policy **while inactive**, then start and service using the prescribed key sequence. An early or malformed service can request reset just as an expired timeout can.

Tiny routes the watchdog request into system reset generation. Its own reset/retention boundary is distinct from the reset it requests; the acceptance application checks retained reset_count on reboot.

Because the watchdog uses the **same AON REF24 clock**, it does not guarantee recovery from a failed AON REF24 clock or provide independent deep-sleep supervision. The current integration is not a safety certificate.
steps: Probe status and inspect retained reset cause before starting a new diagnostic campaign.
Program prescaler, timeout, window and warning policy while inactive.
Start once and service **inside the allowed window** with bounded checks.
After reset distinguish watchdog reboot from fresh power-on and retain diagnostic evidence.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: Pulse Width Modulation (PWM)
summary: Two internal timers and four waveform output channels with capture/fault control.
features: **Four PWM outputs**, two capture inputs and fault/synchronization routes.
Shadow configuration and documented update boundaries.
Runtime PCLK reporting; 24 MHz at SAFE24, updated after RCU transition.
paragraphs: PWM outputs and capture/fault inputs are selected through Tiny GPIO alternate functions. The reusable block has timer/operator state, not an unrestricted programmable I/O processor.

Shadow values become active at the **configured update event**. Writing a duty field alone does not guarantee an immediate glitch-free transition. Establish safe output levels before enabling external power circuitry.

Capture entries and overflow status require coherent reads and **explicit acknowledgement**. Fault handling and debug-halt behavior must be checked with the actual pin route; no electrical frequency limit is qualified here.
steps: Probe ABI and read the actual reported PCLK before timing calculations.
**Keep outputs inactive** while programming timer/operator/channel state.
Latch shadow values at the selected boundary, then enable output routes.
On fault, preserve status and disable/recover outputs before clearing the cause.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: Management UART (UART0)
summary: Primary console UART with 64-byte transmit and receive FIFOs.
features: Fractional baud generation, 5-8 data bits, parity, break and diagnostics.
**GPIO8/9 ALT0 TX/RX**; central-DMA requests 5/6.
Tiny **does not route RTS/CTS**; unsupported flow-control configuration is rejected.
paragraphs: The shared rs_uart_* convenience HAL targets UART0. It is the normal Tiny diagnostic console. Configure baud against the **committed PCLK** and the permitted fractional divider range; sampling margin remains a board/peer requirement.

FIFO acceptance is not completed wire transmission. A UART write timeout can leave a **transmitted/queued prefix**. Preserve protocol framing and inspect RX error flags instead of blindly retrying an entire message.
The polling budget is consumed while the FIFO blocks progress and is shared across the call. It is not a duration in milliseconds and cannot bound a stalled bus access.
steps: Configure baud and framing for the current PCLK with flow control disabled.
Clear stale error/event state and use bounded FIFO operations.
Reserve channel 0 when using UART0 DMA, and follow buffer lifetime rules.
Wait for the required **queue/serializer completion boundary** before changing framing or disabling clocks.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: Inter-Integrated Circuit (I2C0)
summary: One controller-mode I2C instance on GPIO10/11 ALT0.
features: **7-bit and 10-bit addressing**; command and receive FIFOs.
Open-drain SCL/SDA with bounded NACK/error handling.
I2C0 central-DMA requests 7/8; I2C1 is not instantiated.
paragraphs: Only I2C0 is instantiated at 0x10006000, core interrupt input 7. The shared driver supports other product instances, but Tiny rejects I2C1 before MMIO. Its old window and DMA requests are absent.

Program timing against the committed peripheral rate and external pull-ups/capacitance. Clock changes require **idle clients and timing reconfiguration**. A queued command, FIFO empty or DMA transfer return is not automatically completed serial I/O.

Handle NACK, arbitration/bus errors and timeout with explicit status capture and the supported recovery sequence. **Release external SDA/SCL drivers** before alternate-function changes; electrical rise time and peripheral compatibility need board evidence.
steps: Select the bus, verify its GPIO route and calculate timing from the committed PCLK (24 MHz in SAFE24).
Ensure the bus is released, clear stale events and configure supported address mode.
Submit the documented command sequence and inspect **terminal/NACK/arbitration status**.
Recover and release lines before retrying; preserve timeout/error context.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI0)
summary: PCLK-domain master with GPIO-guarded sessions and qualified DMA ports.
features: Master modes 0-3, **8/16-bit frames**, selectable bit order and held-CS segments.
TX-only, RX-only or full duplex; separate eight-word 32-bit FIFOs.
GPIO guard, **session ownership**, finite quotas and V2.2 central-DMA admission.
paragraphs: SPI0 uses GPIO27 ALT0 SCK, GPIO28 ALT1 MOSI and GPIO31 ALT1 CS_N. GPIO30 ALT1 is MISO, or ordinary GPIO D/C in write-only display personality; the personalities are mutually exclusive.

A session is acquired only when GPIO routing and readiness agree. SCK=PCLK/(2*DIV). Configuration changes require the documented **disabled/unowned or clean segment boundary**; HELD and ARMED are not lifecycle-idle states.

Transport packs 8/16-bit wire frames into 32-bit words. FRAME_COUNT defines a finite quota; reject zero and overflow before ARM. Matching request16/17, origin, bound channel, direction and reserved credit are all required at DMA ports. CPU and DMA ports are distinct.

The current raw CAPABILITY value is 0x00003F7F: **DMA discovery bit 7 remains zero** despite the connected Tiny V2.2 DMA path. Treat this as a source/specification discrepancy. Document actual routing and qualified workload evidence separately; this publication does not change the hardware or driver probe.

Successful completion includes **wire completion**, clean packers/FIFOs, fulfilled TX/RX quotas and **drained descriptor/admission/responses**. A software timeout retains all resources. ABORT closes admission; RECOVER and explicit release/reacquisition follow confirmed cleanup.

The ST7789VI-style reference uses 8-bit commands with D/C low and big-endian RGB565 byte streams with D/C high. SPI-P4 covers panel patterns and a sequential capture/verify/display/SD workflow, including direct immutable-PSRAM display and 1024-byte SRAM chunking. It is not parallel video, an arbitrary panel driver or physical panel qualification.
steps: Validate Tiny/DMA identity, select the complete GPIO personality and acquire the session.
Configure timing and finite segment geometry; bind the leased DMA channel before ARM.
Publish immutable data, ARM and START; update D/C **only at clean held-CS boundaries**.
Wait for wire, quotas and drain; on failure retain ownership through abort/recovery, then release explicitly.
evidence: Source reviewed at the publication SHA. Dated phase evidence retains its own source/profile/stage; no new hardware qualification is implied.

title: WS2812 LED Output
summary: Finite RGB LED serializer on GPIO26 ALT0.
features: **24-bit RGB wire frames** on GPIO26 ALT0.
Programmable high/low/reset timing, FIFO watermarks and finite DMA refill.
paragraphs: WS2812 uses PCLK and GPIO26 ALT0. Compute pulse widths from the **actual committed PCLK**; a clock transition cannot interrupt an active wire frame.

Bulk channel 3 remains leased across all refill batches until the **final wire frame and reset interval** complete. DMA completion only proves movement into the controller, not that the LED wire has reached its idle boundary.
The retained P6/P10 model checks cover finite frame/refill workloads. They do not establish arbitrary-strip electrical loading, LED compatibility or uninterrupted output at every clock ratio.
steps: Claim GPIO26 and the bulk channel, then program timing for the current clock.
Fill/arm the finite frame and refill before the bounded service deadline.
Wait for **wire/reset completion**, inspect errors, then release channel and pin ownership.
evidence: Source reviewed at the publication SHA. Dated phase evidence retains its own source/profile/stage; no new hardware qualification is implied.

title: Architecture Information (ARCHINFO)
summary: Read-only Tiny identity and build/configuration discovery.
features: Tiny SOC_ID 0x54494E59; **128 KiB SRAM** and 24 MHz reference clock.
Topology 0x20200001; ICS55 FEATURES0=0x00007FFF and TECHNOLOGY=0x02040037. IHP130 compatibility is 0x00007FFE / 0x02010082.
No provisioned unique device ID is advertised.
paragraphs: The owned Tiny adapter replaces the managed block's fixed SoC identity while retaining its register ABI. BUILD_ID, CONFIG_ID and BUILD_STATUS are supplied by **generated build metadata**; they must not be published as default zero values for a built image.
Read and **validate Tiny identity** before interpreting product-specific capabilities or selecting a firmware layout. The build/profile identity is distinct from a silicon lot/serial number.
Device-ID inputs are tied invalid/read-disabled. Their register offsets do not establish a provisioned unique identity, secure key storage or production traceability.
steps: Read discovery through the SDK and validate the build identity.
Confirm Tiny SOC_ID, one-hart topology, 128 KiB memory and active capabilities.
Reject mismatched images/configurations **before hardware initialization**.
Read device ID only when qualified and enabled; this integration does not supply it.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: System Controller (SYSCTRL)
summary: Tiny-owned control and first-fault/acceptance register bank.
features: Sticky first-fault address, master, response and saturating event count.
CPU/DMA wait-counter snapshot; live/sticky RTC wake status.
**First full-word valid** TEST_STATUS result remains sticky until reset.
paragraphs: Only the decoded Tiny offsets below are implemented. Compatibility identity reads do not create selectable cores, an application processor; clock control is provided by the separate RCU subregion. Other offsets fail; writes to read-only locations, unaligned accesses and partial writes return APB error.

FAULT_STATUS captures the first pending event. Clearing pending permits a subsequent fault record; FAULT_COUNT counts events independently and saturates. Capture address/master/response **before clearing**.
PERF_CTRL controls wait counters and snapshots. Read low/high words from the **captured snapshot**, not from independently changing live values. A wait count is not end-to-end throughput.

TEST_STATUS accepts a full-word write with VALID set only while the prior result is invalid. Reserved input bits are masked; the terminal result is not UART text. A later result **cannot overwrite the first valid one** before reset.

The RCU uses offsets 0x100..0x15C within this same 4 KiB window, through an acknowledged AON crossing. Its independent chapter owns those register definitions; the global address index lists each address once.
steps: Use the Tiny identity before choosing control operations.
Read and preserve pending fault status/address/master/detail **before W1C acknowledgement**.
Enable/capture CPU and DMA wait counters through PERF_CTRL and then read both snapshot words.
For automated acceptance write VALID, PASS and result code once; an earlier failure cannot be replaced by a later pass.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: Reset and Clock Unit (RCU)
summary: AON-domain clock, reset and lifecycle controls inside SYSCTRL.
features: AON-owned profile, gate, reset, cause/fault and CLKOUT controls.
ICS55 **SAFE24 boot with PLL off**; functional PLL192/PLL240 requests.
IHP130 no-PLL compatibility; bounded drain and source recovery.
paragraphs: RCU occupies SYSCTRL+0x100..0x15C (0x1000B100..0x1000B15C), with core input 31. It is a subregion of the existing SYSCTRL window, not another APB address decoder.

AON owns REF24 timekeeping, CLINT and RTC/WDG functional timing. SYS serves CPU/main SRAM/fabric/SDIO; MEM serves XPI; PCLK serves central DMA and peripherals including private Crypto SRAM. AUDIO remains a separate optional source.

ICS55 boots SAFE24 with the PLL parked off. Functional requests select SYS/MEM/PCLK of **192/96/48 MHz or 240/120/60 MHz**. These digital profiles and simulator observations **do not establish a silicon frequency rating**. IHP130 has no PLL; its explicit XIN variants normalize the control reference to 24 MHz.

Clock commands close new admissions, **drain accepted work**, park on REF24, qualify the new source and **publish rate snapshots before reopening**. A failed drain preserves live work. Lock timeout returns SAFE24; stopped PLL recovery uses system/CDC reset, while lost XIN requires restored input and external reset.

Local reset holds five actual leaf edges and waits for synchronized release and bus readiness. SPI and DVP lifecycle, absent AUDIO, held bus responses and active DMA leases retain their endpoint-specific obligations. Current non-CPU commands conservatively drain all central-DMA work.

TARGET_CAP is 0x00037FFF: targets 0..14, SPI0 at 16 and PPALite at 17 are implemented; PIO-lite at 15 is absent. Active PPALite capture rejects clock apply and changed CLKOUT writes. Local gate/reset also requires RAW route, processor/transport idle and source quiet.

Warm system reset returns SAFE24 and resets functional RTC/WDG state while preserving main SRAM contents and recorded cause/fault/debug state. CPU WFI gates only its leaf; unrelated DMA can continue. Clock domains are not independent power islands or an always-powered battery domain.
steps: Read the current profile, rates, target capability and sticky causes.
Stop owners and drain clients; set a nonzero REF24 transition budget.
Submit one supported command and wait with the bounded SDK operation.
Read actual committed profile/rates and faults; reconfigure affected endpoints and **reinitialize PSRAM before reuse**.
evidence: Source reviewed at the publication SHA. Dated phase evidence retains its own source/profile/stage; no new hardware qualification is implied.

title: Local Interrupt Controller (CLINT)
summary: Machine software interrupt and 64-bit timer for hart slot zero.
features: Core interrupt bits 0 and 1 are local software/timer causes.
**1 MHz timebase** derived from AON REF24; unaffected by SYS profile switching.
64-bit time and compare are accessed as RV32 words.
paragraphs: Tiny has one management hart and uses hart slot zero. CLINT is distinct from the external interrupt vector and does not provide a PLIC.
Read time using a **coherent high/low/high retry sequence**. Update compare with the documented **safe word order** so an intermediate value does not trigger an unintended interrupt.
The 1 MHz timebase supports timing measurements/deadlines, while peripheral dividers still use their own committed engine clock. A software busy-loop count is not this timebase.
steps: Use slot zero and the CLINT base from the generated Tiny map.
Read coherent time through the SDK helper.
Mask/prepare the timer cause and update compare in safe word order.
Handle and rearm the **appropriate local cause**; do not subtract two to form an external IRQ ordinal.
evidence: Source reviewed; current-commit matching raw qualification report not supplied.

title: Inter-IC Sound (I2S)
summary: Stereo audio master with PCLK control and a separate AUDIO engine.
features: **Stereo 16/24-bit master** transport; separate TX/RX streams.
PCLK control and asynchronous AUDIO engine with explicit reset readiness.
Channels 6/7 and requests 1/2 by convention.
paragraphs: Tiny integrates the I2S master on GPIO12-17 ALT0. AUDIO is an external/reference clock domain and may be absent at boot; the ordinary CPU release does not wait for it.

Control uses PCLK while serial timing uses AUDIO. The retained acceptance uses 18.432 MHz audio reference; the profile AUD_CLK_HZ setting and actual supplied AUDIO source must be identified separately.

GPIO12-17 overlap the DVP camera profile. **Stop and drain both streams**, release their pads and confirm reset barriers before changing personality. **Missing AUDIO edges** cannot produce a successful engine reset completion.
The integrated serial path is master-only. Generic SDK declarations or a second clock domain do not establish slave mode, continuous underrun-free audio or board codec qualification.
steps: Provide AUDIO and select the **complete ALT0 group**; validate buffer format.
Configure timing and reserve TX/RX channels before starting.
Monitor FIFO and stream errors; stop/drain both directions before route or clock changes.
evidence: Source reviewed at the publication SHA. Dated phase evidence retains its own source/profile/stage; no new hardware qualification is implied.

title: Digital Video Port (DVP)
summary: 8-bit camera capture and crop engine with an asynchronous pixel domain.
features: **8-bit RGB565/YUV422** input with snapshot and crop controls.
GPIO12-23 ALT1 camera profile; asynchronous raw PIXCLK.
DVP_RX request 11 / DMA channel 2; optional initialized XPI PSRAM destination.
paragraphs: DVP at 0x1000E000 uses core input 15 and GPIO12-23 ALT1. GPIO23 is CAM_XCLK from the same RCU CLKOUT generator also routable to GPIO28 ALT0; the two routes are mirrors, not independent clocks.

Snapshot success requires frame completion, DMA completion with the **exact byte count**, **all final destination responses drained** and no DVP/DMA/XPI errors. A frame-done interrupt alone cannot publish a valid frame or justify flushing the tail FIFO.

For RAW capture, even active widths use the DMA helper and odd widths retain the PIO helper. Both RAW helpers reject PROCESS with RS_ENOTSUP. PROCESS uses the PPALite row-aligned transport contract, which also supports odd active widths. A larger allocation never changes the programmed frame length.

Tiny places an exclusive RAW/PROCESS route after the existing payload CDC. PROCESS locks source configuration and observes coherent configuration, error, geometry and sequence handshakes through finalization. rs_dvp_stop is a non-flushing disable/drain operation; ABORT is reserved for ordered failure cleanup. Crop extent must fit the configured frame; dropped-pixel statistics restart for each frame.

Loss of PIXCLK, malformed synchronization, overflow and partial frames invalidate the capture. Preserve diagnostics and bus response obligations during abort/rearm. PCLK/APB stays available without PIXCLK, but engine reset readiness requires the applicable **real clock edges**.
The QVGA/VGA and recovery records are bounded simulator/model results. They do not establish continuous FPS, a sensor register protocol, JPEG encoding or physical camera timing.
steps: Stop conflicting I2S/PWM routes; configure GPIO and inactive CLKOUT before camera enable.
Initialize PSRAM explicitly and validate destination bounds, format, crop and exact byte count.
Start snapshot/DMA2 and wait for every required completion and drain condition.
Stop capture, **verify full frame and guard bytes**, then allow CPU/display/SD consumers.
evidence: Source reviewed at the publication SHA. Dated phase evidence retains its own source/profile/stage; no new hardware qualification is implied.

title: Streaming Pixel Processor (PPALITE)
summary: PCLK camera-stream reduction before the first memory write, with exclusive RAW/PROCESS routing.
features: **One finite frame**; RGB565 byte/channel normalization or YUV422 luma extraction.
Independent **1/2/4 sampling steps**; GRAY8 or RGB565 output with four-byte row alignment.
**Request 11 / DMA2** reuse; APB4 0x1001E000, IRQ27, RCU target 17; no new pins or AXI master.
Two input words, eight output words and a 32-bit packer; **no line or frame RAM**.
paragraphs: Tiny wires the complete P3 path with CAPABILITY=0x000003FF. Reset selects RAW bypass. PROCESS sends the DVP stream through PPALite and returns only that result to the existing DVP_RX endpoint. The two routes are exclusive; there is no simultaneous RAW/processed fanout.

Registers occupy offsets 0x000..0x09C. Accesses must be word-aligned and writes use all four byte strobes. Reads of COMMAND, writes to read-only or undefined offsets, reserved write bits and illegal state/command combinations return an APB error without accepting the operation. IRQ_STATE is write-one-to-clear with simultaneous hardware set taking priority.

All PPALite logic runs in PCLK after the existing DVP PIXCLK-to-PCLK FIFO. Input formats are RGB565_BE=0, RGB565_LE=1, YUYV=2, UYVY=3, YVYU=4 and VYUY=5. PROCESS requires DVP byte/pixel swap disabled and matching post-crop geometry. RGB input supports RGB565 only; YUV input discards chroma and preserves Y without range expansion, producing GRAY8 or replicated gray RGB565.

DVP chronological bytes b0,b1,b2,b3 arrive as {b2,b3,b0,b1}; the first pixel is the low halfword. Canonical RGB565 output places the first pixel low and its low byte in the low memory lane. Optional output byte swap acts within each RGB565 pixel, not across pixels. RGB_SWAP is legal only for RGB input; output byte swap is illegal for GRAY8.

DVP owns cropping. Each input dimension is 1..65535. Step codes 0/1/2 select 1/2/4; code 3 is invalid. Each phase must be smaller than its step and input dimension. Output dimension is ceil((input - phase)/step). Dropped pixels and rows still participate in framing and error checks.

ROW_BYTES is output width times one or two bytes. STRIDE_BYTES rounds each row up to four bytes. VALID_BYTES is ROW_BYTES times output height; TRANSPORT_BYTES is STRIDE_BYTES times output height and EXPECTED_WORDS is transport divided by four. **Padding is per row** and carries zero bytes; consumers must honor stride. A 5x3 YUV source sampled 2x2 to GRAY8 produces 3x2 pixels, six valid bytes, eight transport bytes and two DMA words.

PROCESS admits only direct stream-to-memory request 11 on channel 2 with the exact armed destination and transport count. Wrong channels, mismatched configuration, repeated starts and processed TCDs are rejected. Other requests retain their existing behavior. The DMA channel and all accepted memory responses remain owned until the complete job drains.

**PIPE_DONE is not frame validity.** FINALIZE requires matching source sequence, geometry and raw counts; source stopped without flushing, source quiet, exact DMA completion, terminal response drain and no late source/core/transport error. Only COMPLETE plus RESULT_VALID permits the immutable frame metadata to be consumed.

Route changes require the global DVP/DMA idle barrier; RELEASE keeps the selected route for the next frame. Abort first closes admission and drains accepted DMA work, then isolates and stops/flushes the source, and RECOVER ends ownership only after acknowledgements. **A timeout retains ownership**. Do not reset unrelated DMA or fabricate tail data.

RCU target 17 cannot gate/reset an active processor or a retained PROCESS route. Active capture also prevents clock-profile changes and changed CLKOUT programming; GPIO/DVP/DMA lifecycle barriers remain coupled. P3 integration does not establish camera/display workload qualification, continuous video throughput or physical operating frequency.
steps: Reserve camera pads, CLKOUT, destination storage and DMA2; initialize any PSRAM and select PROCESS while all route participants are idle.
Use rs_ppalite_layout and validate capacity/stride; pass a zero-initialized persistent session to capture_begin. Inspect acquired after any failure.
capture_start starts the exact DMA job before the DVP snapshot. capture_wait stops the source without flushing, checks final counts/errors and performs FINALIZE.
On success, use only the returned valid frame and its stride; release explicitly. On failure, retain the session and storage until bounded abort/recover succeeds.

title: Cryptographic Accelerator (CRYPTO)
summary: Macro-backed AES/SHA2/raw RSA engine with 24 KiB private storage.
features: AES-128/192/256, SHA-224/256 and raw RSA-2048 operations.
**Six private 4 KiB macro banks** on PCLK, separate from the 128 KiB main SRAM.
Central-DMA stream requests 12/13; initialization and explicit scrub/zeroize lifecycle.
paragraphs: Tiny selects the macro-backed Crypto integration with 24 KiB private working storage. This memory does not reduce or extend the CPU-visible main SRAM aperture.

Wait for storage/table initialization and **verified readiness before loading keys** or submitting a job. A capability bit identifies a supported operation, not a completed key load, validated protocol or side-channel qualification.

Channels 4/5 conventionally serve input/output streams. Preserve key, message, result and descriptor ownership until **accelerator completion, DMA completion and final transport drain** agree. Use bounded waits, inspect engine errors and perform the documented zeroize/scrub recovery.

Raw RSA is a modular-arithmetic primitive. Padding, authentication, secure boot, key provisioning and production entropy are application/platform responsibilities; hardware support alone provides none of these guarantees.
steps: Initialize and wait for READY/TABLE_VALID before key and context setup.
Validate operation geometry, reserve streams and publish immutable inputs.
Wait for accelerator and DMA completion; capture errors and result.
Drain, zeroize/scrub when required, and **verify completion before release**.

title: Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC)
summary: Programmable error-detection engine with PIO and coordinated bulk feeds.
features: Programmable CRC width, **polynomial, seed and reflection/byte ordering**.
PIO and coordinated bulk-channel data feeds; no standalone CRC interrupt is wired.
paragraphs: CRC at 0x20006000 provides error-detection arithmetic. CRC is not encryption, authentication or protection against malicious modification.

Configure width, polynomial, seed and byte/reflection order to match the wire or storage format. Preserve the **exact byte sequence** across CPU and DMA feeds; do not compare checksums using incompatible pixel/word byte ordering.

Bulk DMA channel 3 is shared by CRC, XPI, WS2812 and display use by software convention. An application lease lasts through **completion and result capture**; a FIFO or DMA event alone must not transfer ownership to another client.
steps: Acquire any required bulk-channel lease and configure the CRC state.
Feed the exact bounded byte stream **without concurrent writers**.
Wait for completion, read the result and release the lease.

title: Random Number Generator (RNG)
summary: PCLK-domain random-source FIFO and health/control interface.
features: FIFO-based entropy-source interface with **alarms and health status**.
Bounded SDK reads; source quality is an independent integration requirement.
paragraphs: The managed RNG is integrated into Tiny PCLK at 0x20001000. The publication describes its digital FIFO and health/control ABI; it does not certify entropy, unpredictability or cryptographic suitability.

A deterministic verification source and source-level health checks are **not production randomness qualification**. Inspect readiness, startup and health/fault status before consuming data; use the bounded SDK operation and preserve partial/error semantics.
steps: Configure the selected source and alarm policy while idle.
Wait within a bounded budget; inspect health and FIFO state.
On a fault, **stop consumers** and diagnose/reinitialize the source before reuse.
